misconceptions.statement: Chandrayaan-1 found big oceans and lakes of water on the Moon.
misconceptions.why: News headlines said 'water found on Moon' and students picture Earth-like water.
misconceptions.fix: Only small traces of water were found, as hydroxyl and water molecules in soil and as ice in some dark polar craters. There are no oceans or lakes.

probe.question: What did Chandrayaan-1 data show about water on the Moon?
probe.wrong_answer: Large lakes of liquid water on the surface.

misconceptions.root_belief: a headline word means the everyday big version

misconceptions.statement: Liquid water can stay on the Moon's surface because the Moon has water.
misconceptions.why: Students ignore the lack of air pressure and the extreme temperatures.
misconceptions.fix: The Moon has almost no atmosphere, so liquid water would quickly boil away in sunlight or freeze. Water survives only as ice in permanently shadowed places.

probe.question: In what form can water survive on the Moon's polar craters?

misconceptions.statement: Chandrayaan-1 carried a rover that drove around on the Moon.
misconceptions.why: Students merge Chandrayaan-1 with Chandrayaan-3, which showed a rover in news and videos.
misconceptions.fix: Chandrayaan-1 (2008) was an orbiter with a small Moon Impact Probe. It had no rover and did not softly land. The first Indian rover, Pragyan, came with Chandrayaan-3.

probe.question: Which Chandrayaan-1 vehicle drove on the Moon's surface collecting samples?
probe.wrong_answer: Its rover moved on the surface and collected samples.

misconceptions.root_belief: All Chandrayaan missions had the same parts

misconceptions.statement: The Moon Impact Probe landed softly and kept working on the Moon for months.
misconceptions.why: Students think any probe that reaches the Moon lands gently like Vikram.
misconceptions.fix: The Moon Impact Probe was designed to hit the Moon on 14 November 2008. It sent data during its fall and then crashed. It was not a soft lander.

probe.question: How long did the Moon Impact Probe keep working after it reached the Moon's surface?
probe.wrong_answer: It worked for months after landing.

misconceptions.root_belief: Every probe reaching the Moon lands softly

misconceptions.statement: The M3 instrument that found water on the Moon was built by ISRO.
misconceptions.why: Students assume everything on an Indian mission was made by India.
misconceptions.fix: M3 (Moon Mineralogy Mapper) was a NASA instrument flown on Chandrayaan-1. Chandrayaan-1 carried several payloads from other countries, and ISRO built the spacecraft.

probe.question: Which space agency built the M3 instrument that detected hydroxyl on Chandrayaan-1?

misconceptions.root_belief: Indian missions carry only Indian instruments

misconceptions.statement: The water found on the Moon is the same as drinking water and could be drunk straight away.
misconceptions.why: The word 'water' makes students picture ordinary clean liquid water.
misconceptions.fix: Moon water is tiny traces of hydroxyl and water molecules in soil and ice mixed with dust in dark craters. It would have to be collected and purified.

probe.question: Can astronauts drink the Moon's water straight from the ground?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, it is normal water and can be drunk.

misconceptions.root_belief: Water found in space is ready-to-drink liquid

misconceptions.statement: The Chandrayaan-2 orbiter also crashed along with Vikram, so the whole mission failed.
misconceptions.why: News highlighted the lander failure, so students think the entire mission was lost.
misconceptions.fix: Only the Vikram lander lost contact during descent in 2019. The orbiter stayed in orbit around the Moon and continues to study it.

probe.question: What is the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter doing now?
probe.wrong_answer: It crashed with Vikram and is not working.

misconceptions.root_belief: One part failing means the whole mission failed

misconceptions.statement: Vikram of Chandrayaan-2 failed because it ran out of fuel before reaching the Moon.
misconceptions.why: Students guess a simple cause such as fuel for any failure.
misconceptions.fix: Vikram reached close to the Moon and lost contact during the final descent in September 2019. Speed was higher than planned in the last phase. It did not fail on the way to the Moon.

probe.question: At what stage of the journey did Vikram lose contact?
probe.wrong_answer: On the way to the Moon, when it ran out of fuel.

misconceptions.root_belief: Space failures happen due to running out of fuel

misconceptions.statement: Parachutes can be used to slow a lander on the Moon like on Earth.
misconceptions.why: Students know parachutes slow capsules on Earth and forget the Moon has no air.
misconceptions.fix: Parachutes need air to push against. The Moon has almost no atmosphere, so landers use thrusters (rocket engines) firing against the fall.

probe.question: What slows Vikram near the Moon's surface?
probe.wrong_answer: Parachutes open and slow it down.

misconceptions.root_belief: Earth landing methods work on the Moon

misconceptions.statement: A 60 kg person would weigh 60 kg on the Moon because their mass is the same there.
misconceptions.why: Students mix up mass and weight.
misconceptions.fix: Mass stays 60 kg but Moon's gravity is about one-sixth, so the pull (weight) is about one-sixth, like a 10 kg-force.

probe.question: A girl weighs 60 kgf on Earth. About what will she weigh on the Moon?
probe.wrong_answer: 60 kgf, the same as on Earth.

misconceptions.root_belief: Weight and mass are the same quantity

misconceptions.statement: Chandrayaan-3 landed on the far side of the Moon, which never faces Earth.
misconceptions.why: The south pole is mixed up with the far side, and news said 'dark side'.
misconceptions.fix: Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole on the side facing Earth. It is not the far side. Communication was done via the orbiter and Earth stations.

probe.question: On which side of the Moon did Chandrayaan-3 land?
probe.wrong_answer: The far side that we never see from Earth.

misconceptions.root_belief: Polar region means far or dark side

misconceptions.statement: Pragyan kept working on the Moon for many years like a permanent rover.
misconceptions.why: Students expect rovers to run indefinitely, like Mars rovers shown in media.
misconceptions.fix: Chandrayaan-3 was designed for one lunar day (about 14 Earth days). Vikram and Pragyan were put to sleep in September 2023 before the cold lunar night, and did not wake again.

probe.question: For how long was Pragyan designed to work on the Moon?
